verses.text: Jacob also went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
When Jacob saw them, he said, "This is God's camp!" So he named that place Mahanaim, which means "two camps".
Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.
He told them, "This is what you must say to my master Esau: 'Your servant Jacob says, I have been staying with Laban and have remained there until now.
I have cattle and donkeys, sheep and goats, and male and female servants. Now I am sending this message to my master, hoping that you will be kind to me.'"
When the messengers came back to Jacob, they said, "We went to your brother Esau, and now he is coming to meet you, with four hundred men."
Jacob was very afraid and worried. So he divided the people who were with him into two groups, and the flocks and herds and camels as well.
He thought, "If Esau comes and attacks one group, the group that is left may escape."
Then Jacob prayed, "O God of my grandfather Abraham and God of my father Isaac, O LORD, you told me, 'Go back to your country and your relatives, and I will make you do well.'
I am not worthy of all the kindness and faithfulness you have shown your servant. When I crossed this Jordan River, I had only my walking stick. But now I have become two camps.
Please save me from the hand of my brother Esau. I am afraid that he will come and attack me, and the mothers with their children too.
But you have said, 'I will surely make you do well, and I will make your descendants like the sand of the sea, which is too much to count.'"
Jacob spent the night there. Then from what he had with him he chose a gift for his brother Esau:
two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred female sheep and twenty rams,
thirty female camels with their young, forty cows and ten bulls, and twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys.
He put each herd in the care of one of his servants and said to them, "Go on ahead of me, and keep some space between the herds."
He told the servant in front, "When my brother Esau meets you and asks, 'Who is your master? Where are you going? Who owns all these animals in front of you?'
then you must say, 'They belong to your servant Jacob. They are a gift sent to my master Esau, and Jacob himself is coming behind us.'"
He gave the same instructions to the second servant, the third, and all the others who followed the herds. He said, "You must say the same thing to Esau when you meet him.
And be sure to say, 'Your servant Jacob is coming behind us.'" Jacob thought, "I will calm him down with these gifts I am sending on ahead. Later, when I see him, perhaps he will welcome me."
So Jacob's gifts went on ahead of him, but he himself spent the night in the camp.
That night Jacob got up and took his two wives, his two slave women and his eleven sons, and crossed the river Jabbok at the shallow place.
After he had sent them across the stream, he sent over everything he owned.
So Jacob was left alone. Then a man wrestled with him until daybreak.
When the man saw that he could not win, he touched the socket of Jacob's hip, and Jacob's hip was put out of joint as he wrestled with the man.
Then the man said, "Let me go, because it is daybreak." But Jacob replied, "I will not let you go unless you bless me."
The man asked him, "What is your name?" "Jacob," he answered.
Then the man said, "Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, which means 'he struggles with God', because you have struggled with God and with people, and you have won."
Jacob said, "Please tell me your name." But he replied, "Why do you ask my name?" Then he blessed him there.
So Jacob named the place Peniel, which means "face of God". He said, "I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared."
The sun rose above him as he passed Peniel, and he was limping because of his hip.
That is why, to this day, the people of Israel do not eat the muscle attached to the socket of the hip, because the socket of Jacob's hip was touched near that muscle.
